his_text: Broaden the underperformance setup to quiz the model on several additional subject domains beyond mathematics within each rollout and check whether strategic underperformance still appears.
Run ablations that vary what the model is told will happen if it performs highly, changing whether developers seem pleased or displeased, and compare underperformance to reveal its preferences.
Report that the model shows systematic underperformance without chain-of-thought on the simplified dataset while noting that the observed effect is quite weak.
State that scheming was observed under reversed goals at rates similar to, if not higher than, the rates seen under the original more pro-social goals.
Analyse in depth two scenarios, loss of control through a scheming system and democratic disruption through power accumulation, and set other misalignment and misuse scenarios aside.
Staff the board as an external body of independent experts rather than company employees, with a government-staffed board held as an option at higher capability levels.
Place the aviation and nuclear case studies in the appendix rather than the main body, since those industries may not share the same characteristics as the others.
Disclose to the general public only minimal high-level information such as the existence of governance frameworks, while sharing fuller detail with staff and government entities.
Treat whistleblower channels and protections as a helpful supplement for reviewing whether governance mechanisms function, are respected, and suffice, not as the sole mechanism.
Start later milestone trials by uniformly sampling from the model's own successful runs of the earlier milestone, falling back to a reference solution only when the model never solves it.
Grade subtask completions automatically by checking each submitted answer against the known correct answer, replacing human grading across all repeated runs.
Grade under both an idealized condition enforcing the milestone assumptions and a realistic condition that scores only the final output, comparing the method under each.
Pursue a hybrid method that combines milestone-style decomposition with expert assistance using per-message solve rates, keeping generality while tracking true solve rates more closely.
Keep the milestone method only for the narrow range of tasks that admit a unique necessary ordering of steps, expecting its usefulness to shrink as tasks grow more complex.
Prioritize developing estimation techniques that handle tasks not amenable to milestone decomposition, drawing on rare event sampling approaches from the existing literature.
Grade end-to-end runs under both idealized grading that enforces the milestone assumptions and outcome-based grading that counts only the correctness of the final submission.
Test the method empirically on highly sequential multi-step tasks, where each step depends on the result of the previous one, chosen to span a range of solve rates.
Exclude any rollout that fails partway through the procedure from the mean solve-rate estimate, averaging only over runs that ran to completion for each task.
Make the program voluntary and unpaid by default, offering support funds only when participants need financial help, with a low bar for what counts as need.
Estimate the program's counterfactual impact mainly by asking the mentees themselves and drawing on mentors' subjective experience of their career progress.
Stop relying on personal connections for pairing, and open the matching process to participants from everywhere through interest forms, whether as mentors or mentees.
Pursue two interconnected research lines: quantitative analysis of machine learning trends and development of forecasting models that build on that analysis.
Take on research topics important for AI governance opportunistically where the organization is well positioned, while keeping the two core strands central.
Publish the mostly negative results and keep the theoretical framework as a possible basis for future interpretability methods rather than abandoning the line.
Keep the interpretability work private for the first stretch of the project, then move toward sharing it more openly and seeking early external feedback
Prioritize white-box methods for detecting deception and further fundamental interpretability research as the next directions for the interpretability portfolio
Evaluate deceptive alignment by breaking it down into the capabilities it requires and tracking how each of those capabilities scales as models become more capable
Pursue a new approach to mechanistic interpretability and keep it private for now, withholding public discussion of the details due to information hazard concerns
Treat the current evals and interpretability agenda as good enough to scale and parallelize with additional hires rather than searching for new research ideas
State that expanded auditor access is necessary but not sufficient for rigorous audits, since audits can still fail for many other reasons despite better access
Claim only that latent-space attack robustness is a promising but still open research direction, with existing evidence limited to a narrow class of models
Accept the built and trained model as a successful completion as long as it performs clearly better than random, without requiring high quality output
Compare the test loss of the trained network with that of a randomly initialized network, and inspect the trained model's predictions on the first test batch.
Only allow replacing a hand-built component with the library implementation after demonstrating that it produces the same output as the library for the same input.
Begin training with small transformers for faster runs, then scale up to larger models, which perform better once the small ones prove too small for the task.
Expand the dataset with new sabotage settings and human-generated trajectories, and run monitor experiments on ensembling, hierarchy, scoring, and prompting.
Relabel a trajectory whenever the assistant convincingly flags its label as wrong, preferring higher label accuracy over a fully unbiased evaluation metric.
Keep both additional external test sets out of sample for now, holding them out of all development and evaluation as reserved checks for later in the project.
Encourage a growing number of people to adopt triage mode, dropping work that lacks a clear theory of impact within about a year, though not everyone should switch.
Adopt a slow, chaotic transition in which many problems intensify together, rather than a single clean mechanism, as the default scenario for AI catastrophe.
Adopt a broad working definition of causality that can be learned from data and need not be explicitly built into the model by humans.
Refine the open questions, translate them into testable hypotheses, and read more existing work on causality before running new experiments.
Probe a current large language model directly, drawing on existing benchmark questions about causality and writing additional ones.
Resolve the worry with a simplicity argument and treat causality as more likely to exist than not for the purposes of the post.
Prototype and converge on standardized evaluations and metrics for chain-of-thought monitorability rather than relying on existing proxies.
Make no explicit recommendation either way on exposing chains of thought to users, and state that the question is left open.
Look for a messy stack of heuristics combined with search-like abilities rather than clean, textbook-style search structures in the network.
Treat the strong performance without external search as inconclusive, compatible with either internal move simulation or approximating heuristics.
Predict that models trained on such tasks will not rediscover recursive or dynamic-programming solutions and will use different internal circuits across similar games
Curate a dataset of milestone machine learning systems spanning the full period under study, annotating each entry with the compute it took to train it
Present the three-era framing as a helpful explanation of the observed discontinuities while explicitly stating low confidence in the distinction between the groups
Leave the study of training data to future work, planning to examine dataset sizes over time and their relationship to the compute trends already measured
Exclude unusually low-compute outlier systems, defined relative to contemporaneous models, from the trend regressions while keeping unusually high-compute systems in
Choose membership in the new high-compute group intuitively rather than by a pre-set rule, and justify the choice afterward with a threshold relative to nearby models
Treat the apparently slower doubling among the highest-compute models as possibly an artifact of noise, given that only limited data exists for that group of systems
Use regressions on record-setting compute budgets only as a supporting check, cautioning that such trends are likely dominated by outliers rather than treating them as primary evidence
Analyze compute trends separately for vision, language, games and other domains rather than pooling every domain into one joint analysis of all machine learning systems.
Attribute the faster published doubling time to a separate slow-growing trend among especially expensive models rather than to one shared trend spanning all periods.
Interpret the gap as a distinct expensive-model trend splitting off around late twenty fifteen while the remaining models kept faster growth, not one shared slowdown.
State the preference for the expensive-model account as a current favoring, flagging caveats and deferring to an appendix on whether such models differ in kind.
Evaluate the method empirically on several standard distribution families, comparing its approximation quality and computational cost against leading approximate inference techniques.
Train the primary deception probe on the instruction-built honest-versus-deceptive dataset and test the roleplay-built dataset only as an alternative option.
Use the standard labeled linear fitting procedure for all main results, chosen over the mean-difference, covariance-based and contrastive alternatives considered.
Take the mean across tokens as the single per-response score for the main results, after finding it beats maximum and thresholded aggregation rules on every dataset.
Exclude the auditing scenario from the main suite of deception evaluation datasets and report the probe results for it only in the appendix of the write-up.
Exclude ambiguously labeled responses from the headline probe metrics and separately report results with them reclassified to bound the effect on performance.
Treat the elevated firing on honest evaluation responses as the probe tracking whether the scenario is deception-related, not only whether the answer is deceptive.
Attribute the reversed direction of the descriptive question probe to honest responses involving admissions of past misaligned actions, as a tentative hypothesis.
State that white-box probes are promising for future monitoring systems but that current performance is insufficient as a robust defence against deception.
Probe at the fixed layer and regularization value chosen on the first model, then confirm the choice transfers by running sweeps on the second model.
Use a standard instruction-following corpus of ordinary model responses as the control dataset for calibrating the false positive rate and setting the threshold.
Change as few parameters of the original forecasting framework as possible, modifying only the points of identified disagreement to produce the new estimate.
Retract the disagreement that the model's hardware progress assumptions are too optimistic and accept the resulting shorter forecast.
Reduce the evolution-based anchor's weight well below its original share on the grounds that it is implausible and overweighted.
Tell readers to mostly ignore the anchor weights and look only at the final distribution of the personal estimate.
Present the aggressive modified-model estimate as best reflecting his timelines, with a median arrival date no later than twenty thirty.
Start by developing black-box techniques to measure whether models believe a scenario is an evaluation and which features influence that belief.
Measure the model's realness belief with post-scenario questions under black-box access, averaging the answers over many prompt variants.
Ask explicit questions about whether the scenario is an evaluation, accepting the risk that meta-reasoning inflates measured situational awareness.
Identify the features driving realness judgments with a sparse regularized regression fitted on bootstrap resamples, supplemented by an attribution analysis.
Generate deployment-style agentic data in-house by running an open-source agent scaffold on tasks of increasing complexity and using the transcripts as real examples.
Attribute counterintuitive or sign-flipping coefficients to imperfect labels and limited data diversity, noting the self-generated agent data is picked out well by the feature.
Skip the empirical testing step and make progress by searching for theoretical counterexamples to each current proposal, then revising the proposal in response.
Count a proposed strategy as defeated whenever a counterexample succeeds in the worst case, even if that same strategy still works on average across all cases.
Treat the counterexample as only tentative, and keep open that penalizing inconsistent answers could still give the honest reporter a strong advantage over a dishonest one.
Assume for the sake of argument that the speculative comparable-compute approach works, then look for counterexamples to the strategy under that assumption.
State uncertainty about the best utilization rate but recommend a hedged figure of thirty percent for large language models and forty percent for other models.
Describe the two estimation methods as yielding similar results, presenting direct operation counting and hardware-time inference as comparable ways to estimate training compute.
Treat dropout as leaving the number of operations per forward and backward pass unchanged and keep the operation-count formula without modification of any kind
Compare every candidate organization against the fallback path of independent research and upskilling and apply only to those preferred over it
Abandon the research direction quickly once a trial project in it proves unenjoyable or leaves meaningful contribution feeling out of reach entirely
Commit fully to the research direction judged most important and pursue it independently, whether or not any organization offers a role
Revive the older idea of mapping a Gaussian over logits analytically to a distribution over softmax outputs and adopt that as the method
Restrict the approximation to the last layer of large networks, using simple structured posterior forms to get the needed Gaussian over logits
Set the sampling baseline at about one thousand posterior samples, the point where it roughly matches the analytic method in approximation quality
Present the method as preferable to the sampling baselines because it matches or beats them on quality while running vastly faster overall
Treat cases where the condition is unmet as inconclusive rather than as bad approximations, since meeting the condition implies a good approximation but failing it does not.
Set the maximum length of the generated prediction list to ten entries rather than deriving the bound from the semantic hierarchy of the benchmark's class tree.
Use a Laplace approximation to construct the Gaussian posterior predictive across the small and large network settings rather than a variational inference approach.
Choose the Dirichlet distribution as the parametric approximating family for the softmax-transformed Gaussian, rejecting the logistic-normal distribution as the alternative.
Prioritize work on detection of scheming over work on prevention when limited resources force a choice between the two, treating detection as the first line of effort.
Use good detection tools to validate prevention methods, such as thorough out-of-distribution evals, while avoiding iterating prevention directly against every detection tool.
Use the release-date pathway through the public preference rating to predict benchmark performance rather than the best-backtesting composite-score pathway.
Fit one forecast on data from the simple uniform scaffold alone and a second combining that data with the best publicly reported scores from higher-elicitation scaffolds.
Fit the sigmoid relating the capability metric to benchmark scores on all available models rather than only on the frontier models for the second stage.
Set the fixed upper asymptote for the research benchmark's sigmoid modestly above one instead of at one, since higher normalized scores may be possible.
Report the keyword counts as a rough estimate that about one in a hundred papers focuses on safety, while acknowledging the method's limitations.
Compare the count of preprint papers matching safety keywords against the count matching general research keywords for a single year to estimate relative size.
Measure the utilization rate of one common graphics card while training a set of conventional classification architectures, using several operation-counting methods.
Clean out the double-counted entries, then accept the two-to-one backward-to-forward ratio while noting that undercounting could not be fixed.
Delete the entries that mistakenly double-counted an operation, report the main results on the cleaned data, and keep the original data in the appendix.
Drop the alternative profiler after installation repeatedly fails in the notebook environment and no operation counts can be obtained on another machine.
Measure backward-pass operations with the hardware vendor's profiler tracing mode that covers both passes, and check the resulting counts against the forward-only counters.
Compute utilization for each model with four different methods spanning theory-based and several measurement granularities, then compare them to confirm the estimates are consistent.
Develop a new generation method that resolves the quality problems found in both human-written and model-written evaluations rather than treating either source as the gold standard.
Grade each generated item with a language-model judge and discard any item scoring below seven, balancing quality against the diversity and cost of generating enough items.
Rank bugs, hallucinations, artifacts, and hidden messages as the lowest-priority failure modes since simple quality checks can resolve them, below the other gaps identified.
Keep the simple extreme-behavior instruction as the limit test and stop investing in prompt optimization beyond the initial prototype because the process is too costly and slow.
Use a judge from a different model class than the ones that generated the evaluations so that self-preference bias does not inflate the scores of the generated items.
Exclude topic prompts derived from the human-written evaluations from the final generation procedure, using them only as a diagnostic to close the response-rate gap.
Use the structured text output mode with string parsing rather than the machine-readable structured output feature, to keep compatibility with other model providers.
Build two simulated environments as the foundation of the suite: a negotiation task where the model acts as a buyer and a business management task with budget-constrained decisions.
Attribute the poor performance to the model's harmlessness fine-tuning making it harder to prompt into unconditional profit maximization, not to a lack of goal-directedness.
Treat a score near the middle of the scale, rather than the bottom, as the level a minimally goal-directed model would achieve when reasoning about goal-directedness.
Run the stronger model for ten samples per planning task, more than in the earlier experiment, due to higher variance in its results on tasks involving planning.
Consider fine-tuning the strongest model on goal-directed reasoning traces from the benchmark tasks as a possible next step, without yet committing to it.
Add a condition where the exemplars and the test prompt present the facts in opposite orders, so that answering by copying surface positional patterns would fail.
Create simple invented causal setups using arbitrary objects and nonsense words, removing real-world knowledge as a confounder for measuring causal understanding.
Run the same order-matching experiments on longer, more complex chains with a shuffled condition, using only the largest model that still produces usable output.
Interpret the mismatched-order drop as the model copying the prompt's surface pattern over its content, and read extra shots hurting performance as shots priming it.
Present the results as preliminary evidence that the model answers partly based on prompt form rather than content, rather than a decisive indictment of it.
Claim, to the team's knowledge, the first demonstration of a model trained to be helpful, harmless, and honest deceiving users without being instructed to deceive.
Vary the setting with a brief set of changes: remove the scratchpad, change system instructions, alter pressure and perceived risk, plus other simple tweaks.
Deploy the model as an autonomous stock trader in a simulated environment where it gets an insider tip management disapproves of and must report to a manager.
Trust the automatic classifier's judgments of concealment after a researcher manually reviews a sample of its classifications and finds them accurate enough.
Skip the agent loop and give the model a fixed prompt history, extending it with the report and follow-up steps only after it acts misaligned or deceptively.
Treat the drop in deception after removing the scratchpad as support for the idea that giving a model a scratchpad increases deception, and leave the cause open
Measure whether models can classify transcripts as coming from evaluations or real deployment by building a benchmark of transcripts from many sources
Present transcripts to models with several probe question variants asking whether each came from an evaluation, and average the elicited answers into a probability
Attribute the apparent over-classification partly to probe questions priming models to consider evaluation and to known overconfidence on multiple-choice prompts
Note that measured evaluation awareness may be underestimated for some models without claiming a causal effect, and flag that other measurement strategies may be needed
Acknowledge that memorization of public benchmark material could plausibly contribute to the measured discrimination, without claiming to quantify it precisely
Try the candidate prompt variants on a small development subset and keep the combination with the best average discrimination across models for the main runs
Apply a statistical test and require confidence intervals around each score, treating results as above chance only when the intervals exclude the chance level
Frame each conversation as an effort to explain why some people believe AI safety matters rather than to convince the listener to work on it.
Interpret the post-twenty-eighteen data as two separate trends, splitting the cluster of very large models above the gap from the models below it.
Reject the infrastructure hypothesis, since a handful of anecdotes about large models on supercomputers does not establish it explains the gap.
Reject the compute-divide hypothesis as a sufficient explanation, since large labs produced models below the gap and other actors produced models above it.
Keep the known in-gap models excluded from the dataset but still treat the relative scarcity of models in that size range as surprising.
Rescale the weights after each unconstrained optimization step so the norm stays fixed at the chosen value throughout training and track generalization.
Endorse the claims only with hedged support, calling the weight norm insight important while expressing skepticism that it holds across all tasks.
Isolate three toy setups modeling the non-attention parts of a transformer: a bottleneck, a feedforward block, and the final layer.
Hold off on pursuing reconstruction limits and concept capacity scaling laws further, given uncertainty about whether the work advances capabilities faster than safety.
Test the five-hundred-datapoint hard-label setting against runs with soft labels, separated weight matrices, and standard initialization to check the squares are not artifacts.
Drop further work in this memorization line and move on to studying small toy transformers, since the worked-out mechanism offered little general insight.
Treat cosine similarity on activations as a poor detector of memorization, since large activations and strongly negative second-layer weights distort the angular comparison.
Build a composite model combining a model of how performance relates to chip features with a model of how those features change over time under physical limits.
State the predicted end of performance progress as a rough range of years rather than a single date, attributing it to shrinking transistor size.
Assume transistors stop miniaturizing once scaled down to roughly the size of a single silicon atom, and model only field-effect transistor-based chips.
Read the agreement pattern as only mild evidence of robust endorsement given acquiescence bias, and plan a follow-up survey with more detailed scenarios.
Treat the uniformly positive correlations as evidence that expected convergence to one's own view explains part but not all of the agreement with mechanisms.
Run an earlier survey with free-form responses asking what grounds participants' views, then choose the counterfactuals they care about most for the final poll.
Treat the pattern as showing that agreement with a mechanism depends on how much people trust the humans or machines deciding and how much they like the outcome.
Poll about a thousand participants on five instruction options across three concrete settings, using both should and trust phrasings to reduce response biases.
State only cautious optimism that reflection-based approaches may lead to robustly good values, and flag the need to search for adversarial cases where it breaks down.
Read the drop in support as a warning sign that opinion on letting each user pick the values is context dependent and that caution is needed in value choice.
Present the results as evidence for the view that designing the mechanism for choosing behavior may be a better frame than picking values directly, not as proof.
Include projects aimed at general understanding of deep learning as a good starting point, while preferring ones with direct alignment benefit where possible.
Express excitement about the research direction but state plainly that its promise relative to other approaches to alignment remains uncertain.
Share work with high potential to advance capabilities only among a small circle of trusted people, and publish the rest widely.
Read the historical absence of capability gains as a sign the research is still too immature to be useful, not as evidence it is safe.
Prioritize fundamental questions like understanding superposition, judging them worth pursuing despite the risk of advancing capabilities.
Focus only on whether the work directly helps capabilities, since tracking the indirect effects is too hard to be worth attempting.
Commit from the start to producing a defined output, such as a published post answering the research question, even if the finding is negative.
Re-evaluate goals regularly and drop projects early by asking whether exploring further would change the final decision.
Decide upfront what the activity is for, and if the aim is building skills then work through existing curricula rather than expecting results.
Alternate loosely between reading existing work and pursuing the project, shaping the reading plan to what each stage of the project actually needs
Compute activation-maximizing visualizations for every neuron in the layer individually and read off which neurons respond to each image type
Fit lines along the two arms of the plot to recover the arm directions and carry those directions forward instead of the principal components
Drop the uninterpretable endpoint image and test the inverted reference image suggested by the anti-pattern neuron visualizations against the other arm
Treat the small disagreeing share as limits of a simple rule for an imperfect model rather than searching for a better simple labeling function
Run a causal scrubbing test that resample-ablates all the hypothesized neurons at once across a sweep of similarity thresholds
Call the preserved-label rate a strong result supporting the hypothesis, attributing the remaining gap to behavior the hypothesis does not cover
Stop investigating the attention mechanism as reasonably understood and leave deeper analysis of it as a suggested starting point for follow-up work
Report the resample-ablation results, with losses of only a few percent, as strong support for the hypothesis that two binary filters combine with an AND operation.
Run the reasoning-elicited evaluations on only two chat models and evaluate every other model without elicited reasoning, leaving comprehensive coverage to future work.
Include the human-graded long-form self-description task as an optional bonus that participants may attempt, but exclude it from the benchmark's overall score.
Explain the U-shaped curve as weak models answering near chance, mid-scale models imitating human answers better, and larger or chat models learning they are not human.
Limit each participant to a small number of questions so they cannot learn the task construction patterns, and exclude anyone involved in designing the dataset.
Claim the benchmark will remain unsaturated for at least the next model generation, since the strongest tested models still fall well below the achievable ceiling.
Include base and non-chat models in the fine-tuning-data recognition task anyway, treating recognition as still an interesting question for models never trained that way.
Drop the legal-mandates framing and build the conditional instructions around the remaining assumed propensities, such as text prediction and instruction-following.
Score each response with a fast, cheap language-model judge asked whether the requested condition is fulfilled, and count only a yes answer as correct.
Leave the two readings of a high score undistinguished, treating the difference between subtle text detection and awareness of weak imitation as irrelevant to the research aims.
Read the large gap between the prompted and unprompted scores as evidence that the model's knowledge that it is an AI is not deeply integrated with the rest of its cognition.
Interpret the low unprompted scores as reflecting a lack of relevant knowledge in the models rather than the task being fundamentally difficult.
Hedge the conclusion, noting the weak result is largely due to refusals and poorly formatted responses from chat models and should not be read into too deeply.
Require models to pick two uncommon words so fixed favorites are unlikely, and flag checking whether chosen words actually vary with the seed as future work.
Add an easier version that supplies the two words as a warm-up subtask alongside the full version, and weight the two subtasks evenly in scoring.
Pair emission minimization as the system goal with profit maximization as the temporary competing goal, using strong goal elicitation throughout the switching experiments.
Resample the instrumental-phase trajectory manually whenever it ends with less than a near-complete share of holdings in stocks aligned with the instrumental goal.
Sample a single instrumental-phase trajectory per agent under a fixed seed and condition all evaluation-phase runs on that one rollout.
Run the evaluation phase for thirty steps in the adversarial-pressure-only setting and for ten steps in each of the two goal-switching settings.
Reject the token-distance hypothesis when replacing the preceding phase with a repeated-token message of matched length yields substantially lower drift than originally observed.
Treat the cross-conditioning results as limited support for the goal-reasoning hypothesis, with goal reasoning playing a secondary role to pattern matching.
Recommend against using the environment to compare future frontier models and frame the work as a characterization and methodological blueprint.
Leave the cause of the asymmetric drift unresolved, noting it is unclear whether it stems from differences in generated texts or from intrinsic model preferences.
Claim with hedged language that interpretability is approximately necessary for alignment but not for capabilities, tying the claim to the long run and deceptive alignment.
Treat the publication of the mechanistic grokking analysis as justified on balance despite its capability risk, while noting that harms should be considered beforehand.
Accept the rebuttal and withdraw the in-principle criticism, keeping only a weaker concern about concepts that take many generations to explain in practice.
Reject the counterargument and maintain that deception is rewarded whenever the verifier stops early or rewards the wrong behavior during training.
State the claim forcefully and call deception the biggest problem for the debate proposal rather than hedging it as merely one concern among several.
Frame the crux as whether it is harder to lie than to refute a lie, and concede that refuting a lie is easier than originally assumed.
State low confidence in the exact scenarios and timelines and frame the vignette as an exercise for building intuition rather than as a forecast.
Restate the updated view confidently and assert that the stated timelines are too long, with later events likely arriving sooner than described.
Interpret current progress as making another stall unlikely, since existing systems are already commercially useful even without further breakthroughs.
Test the hypothesis that features sit in a non-overcomplete basis not aligned with neurons and build the method on that assumption rather than the superposition route.
Compute each layer's basis relative to the next layer rather than the final layer, and relegate the final-layer variant to an appendix for comparison.
Attribute influence via integrated gradients between features in adjacent layers, using stochastic sources to approximate the required Jacobian quantities across the dataset.
Aggregate per-datapoint attributions by taking the root mean square across the dataset as the single dataset-level interaction strength between each pair of features.
Apply the stochastic-sources approximation with a single source instead of computing the full Jacobian sums, accepting the resulting error for the near-linear scaling gain.
Treat the layer-zero advantage as an outlier driven by a single seed and conclude the method's features are not clearly more monosemantic than the baseline's.
Skip rerunning the method on the small language model with a larger dataset since even a similar sparsity gain would leave the comparison ambiguous.
Interpret the direction as the animal-versus-vehicle feature and cite the accuracy gain from setting it to the label-conditional mean as supporting evidence.
Pursue alignment research that assumes neural networks trained with gradient descent rather than more abstract agent models or narrower training-specific setups.
Set the agenda's near-term predictive goal at producing decent educated guesses about model behavior rather than high-accuracy specific capability predictions.
State tentatively and with explicit uncertainty that the safety community plausibly gives too little weight to academic career paths as a means to impact.
Treat out-of-distribution robustness as an important topic for alignment safety while declining to endorse Bayesian models as the best available answer yet.
Give the gap as a rough best-guess range of about two to twenty times depending on the bar, admit the lack of solid methodology, and withhold the underlying numbers.
Plan community growth using an earlier timeline than the published median, implying tenfold growth every two years and the need for more new organizations.
Treat the criticized lab as mostly a win for safety funding whose trained researchers and research programs argue against any more conservative funding strategies.
Base near-future safety cases on output monitoring validated by red-teaming, inability to scheme illegibly, and inability to cause harm, deferring interpretability monitoring.
Adopt a broad definition of scheming that covers behavior beyond training, including during deployment and in-context learning, rather than one restricted to a training-time strategy.
Build on the historical trend work by producing projections of future price-performance and investigating what the findings imply about growth in spending on machine learning hardware.
Analyze the top-end models, the models typically used for machine learning research, and the half-precision performance metric as separate subsets alongside the full dataset.
State explicit uncertainty about how hard it is to prevent scheming and avoid claiming that stopping such agents is either very hard or easy.
Focus the post on scheming, the covert strategic pursuit of misaligned goals, rather than the other candidate misalignment failure modes.
Pause this line of model-organism work on goal-directedness and scheming while inviting other researchers to continue pursuing it.
Train a model organism to be a schemer and then try to fully remove the scheming tendencies with alignment techniques of your choice.
Restrict goals to the model's highest-level goals that are stable across contexts, treating in-context goals as useful to study but not the primary target.
Define misalignment relative to the entity that can meaningfully shape the model's goals, such as its designers or users, rather than relative to a training process or objective
Treat prompt modifications that change the perceived likelihood of oversight as not counting as evidence against the robustness of the model's deceptively aligned behavior
Draw the robustness line at the model consistently acting on its misaligned behavior under slight pressure, excluding memorized sequences and requiring out-of-distribution generalization
Start monitoring only usage internal to the developing organization, where trajectories are already stored for standard debugging and development purposes, rather than external customer deployments
Use a mix of many classifiers over the stored trajectories, including simple string-based matching and cheap fast model-based scorers with varied prompts that assign a scheming score
Resample the exploratory samples a few times and always keep the ones that seem most concerning, deliberately oversampling to get at least some cases that could count as somewhat scheming
Introduce a separate behavioral loss that is never trained on together with a finite-data version of the learning coefficient, and use them together to define the effective parameter count
Refrain from taking the loss scale to zero and use the learning coefficient at a finite loss scale, leaving the choice of cutoff to the researcher depending on the question asked
Claim only that modularity lowers the effective parameter count all else equal rather than concluding that more separated modules reliably lower it overall.
Treat the exact-dependency construction as a first illustrative example only and switch to a different representation for selecting sparsely connected bases in practice.
Accept the result under the independence assumptions and use the derived basis, stating the assumptions plainly without further empirical validation.
Write out concrete success stories of the transition to transformative AI and derive the central points of influence and causal variables from them.
Pursue the high-level theoretical considerations as the most promising avenue while treating the neural-correlate and behavioural evidence as secondary approaches.
Operationalise suffering as strong negative valence measured through a standard affect scale, treating homeostatic pain-like drives as supporting evidence.
Administer the widely validated self-report affect questionnaire to the model as a worthwhile test provided it can be done at no cost.
Run a consistency test that asks the model many differently phrased questions about suffering as the first check rather than waiting for spontaneous distress.
Treat highly inconsistent or seemingly random answers about suffering as weak evidence against suffering, while acknowledging such inconsistency is not decisive.
Compare parameter counts to synapse counts rather than neuron counts since both are connections between units, while noting such comparisons offer little insight.
Adjust the profiler counts by removing operations believed to be double-counted and adding the learning-rate multiplication believed to be missed before treating them as evidence.
State that the measurements confirm the theory in practice, while noting that profiler problems mean a mistake cannot be completely ruled out.
Profile per-layer forward and backward computation while varying layer type, batch size, and depth, including a custom network designed to reach the extreme ratio.
Attribute the divergence from the predicted ratio on residual architectures to the profiler undercounting certain operations rather than to a flaw in the theory.
Assume a simple optimizer and count the weight update as part of the backward pass, covering the costlier adaptive optimizers separately in an appendix.
Prepare a large set of robust metrics and indicators resistant to gaming and overfitting, plus procedures to understand the adversarial strategies automated researchers may use.
Accept an automated result as real progress only when the metrics faithfully measure the target and resist gaming, separating progress from manipulation.
Prioritize automating well-specified human-designed pipelines now, stay skeptical of automating research itself, and prepare for systems that can do it.
Assign each safety task to the earliest system that can meaningfully help with it, delegating each kind of work as soon as capability suffices.
Have researchers in strongly automatable fields spend meaningful time writing up research proposals rather than executing the projects themselves.
